DI DACONO P'L'P'NAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City www dilg,gov.ph OPINION NO. s. 20?5 FEB 2 6 2025 HON. REX R. JALANDO-ON, MO, MPM City Mayor City of La Carlota Negros Occidental Dear Mayor Jalando-on: This has reference to your letter dated 16 December 2024 seeking this Departments guidance and legal opinion on this query and we quote: "Hypothetically, if after winning the election on May 10, 2025 and resign as City Mayor on May 15, 2025, before the end of my first term and take my oath for my second term on July 1, 2025, is there any legal impediment for me to assume office and begin my second term considering I resigned on May 15, 2025?" Per the representation, you are currently serving your first term as City Mayor and filed for a second term. You then represented that you have served in the government for more than thirty (30) years. You then stated that your main reason for retiring before your first term ends is to claim your GSIS pension after serving the LGU in various positions for nearly 32 years, and not to potentially extend your constitutionally mandated three-term limit. Thus, the request for legal opinion. At the onset, please be informed that no specific provision under the law that prevents a resigned official from assuming a newly won term. Under Section 81, Article X of the 1987 Constitution, local officials (like mayors) have a three-term limit but resignation shall not be considered as an interruption in the continuity of his service for the full term for which he was elected. Likewise, the Local Government Code (RA 7160) does not disqualify a resigned mayor from assuming a newly won term. 1 Section 8, The term of office of elective local officials, except barangay officials, which shall be determined by law, shall be three years and no such official shall serve for more than three consecutive terms. Voluntary renunciation of the office for any length of time shall not be considered as an interruption in the continuity of his service for the full term for which he was elected. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline NO.: 8876-34-54

The only implication is that resignation before June 30, 2025, would mean the Vice Mayor assumes your position under the succession rule in Section 442 of RA 7160. However, if and when you are elected for your second term (2025-2028), this succession does not affect your right to assume office for your second term on July 1, 2025. Thus, there is no legal impediment preventing you from assuming your second term as City Mayor on July I, 2025, even if you resigned on May 15, 2025. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: . ROMEO P. BENITEZ Undersecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs OUSELLA'RPB/LLLS-LRALLDnasm Sectjon 44. Permanent Vacancies in the Offices Of the Governor, Vice-Govemor, Mayor, and Vice-Mayor. - If a permanent vacancy occurs in the office Of Üle governor or mayor, the vice-governor Or vice-mayor concerned shall become the governor or mayor. If a permanent vacancy occurs in the offices of the governor, vice-governor, mayor, Or vice-mayor, the highest ranking sanggunian member or, in case of his permanent inability, the second highest ranking sanggunian member, shall become the governor, vice-governor, mayor Or vice-mayor, as the case may be. Subsequent vacancies in the said Office shall be filled automatically by the other sanggunian members according to their ranking as defined herein. xxxx Page 2 of 2
